name: nice
description: Starts a program with a modified scheduling priority (niceness). Higher nice value = lower priority.

flags.description: Nice value from -20 (highest priority) to +19 (lowest). Default is +10 when starting a command with nice.
Print the current niceness (same as nice with no arguments).

examples.explanation: Runs a heavy build at the lowest priority so your desktop stays responsive.
Runs a video encode at higher priority. Negative values require root (sudo nice -n -10 ...).
Changes the priority of a RUNNING process (processes cannot lower their own niceness after start; renice can raise it).

about: Niceness is a hint to the kernel scheduler, not a hard limit — a very busy nice-19 process still gets CPU on an idle machine. Only root can decrease niceness (increase priority). CPU share is also governed by cgroups and cpulimit-style tools; nice affects scheduling weight only.
useCases: Run batch jobs without hurting interactive performance.
Give critical tasks a scheduling boost.
mistakes: Expecting nice to limit CPU usage percentage — use cpulimit, cgroups, or systemd resource controls for that.
